newsitem.title: LEBANON: Pope arrives in Lebanon on first Mideast visit.
newsitem.headline: Pope arrives in Lebanon on first Mideast visit.

text.p: Pope John Paul arrived in Lebanon on Saturday on his first visit to the Middle East.
Church bells rang out across the country as his plane landed at Beirut airport, where he was greeted by hundreds of civil and religious dignitaries headed by President Elias Hrawi.
The pope will spend 32 hours in Lebanon on the first visit by a Roman Catholic pontiff to the Middle East since 1964 when Paul VI visited the Holy Land and also made a stop at Beirut airport.
Flag-waving crowds gathered in a holiday atmosphere in Christian districts of Beirut to welcome the pope, but Moslem districts of the Lebanese capital were quieter with few people on the streets.

Hundreds of soldiers in battle fatigues armed with automatic rifles lined the flag-bedecked 10 km (six-mile) road from the airport to the presidential palace where the pope was to travel after being welcomed at the airport.

The pope will meet Moslem leaders and hold a celebration with young people on Saturday evening and an open-air mass on Sunday morning in Beirut's war-ravaged city centre. He is due to return to Rome on Sunday at 7.30 p.m. (1630 GMT).
